summary: feat(bonusly): add `redemptions suggest` -- rewards to redeem again from your own history, next to your current point balance
reason: User asked for a command that suggests redemptions based on the user's point balance. Bonusly's REST v1 API has no rewards-catalog endpoint with prices: README.md's Known Gaps #1 documents that awards/incentives (the closest thing to a claimable-rewards catalog) were live-probed across ~20 path variants each and every one 404'd, and the Redemption type (internal/types/types.go) has no cost field in the confirmed schema. A literal 'what can I afford from the catalog' feature is therefore not buildable without fabricating price data. Scoped with the user (AskUserQuestion) to the buildable alternative: join the live redeemable balance (earning_balance/giving_balance from GET /users/me, the same call promoted_balance.go's `balance` command already makes) against the user's own local redemption history (reward_name/state/created_at, synced via the existing `sync --resources redemptions` path), ranked by times-redeemed then recency. The command explicitly discloses (in --help text, the JSON `note` field, and README/SKILL prose) that it cannot filter by afford-ability, so agent and human callers cannot mistake frequency-ranking for a live price check.
validated_outcome: go build ./..., go vet ./..., and go test ./... all pass (including the new TestNovelRedemptionsSuggestHelpWires wiring smoke test and TestRankRedemptionSuggestions table-driven unit tests). Manually verified `redemptions --help` lists `suggest` alongside `get`/`list-mine`/`forecast`, `redemptions suggest --help` renders the afford-ability disclosure, and `redemptions suggest --dry-run` short-circuits without a network call. No live Bonusly credential was available in this environment to exercise the live balance fetch end-to-end; the same disclosed-untested posture already applies to sibling `pp:data-source auto` novel commands `recognition gap` and `recognition search-mine` (both say 'not yet verified against a real API response in this build' in their own descriptions), and this command's descriptions carry the same caveat.
